November 2, 2026

US said to be preparing renewed strikes on Iran after midterms

tags: war, politics, defence
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell, @oafnation_actual

The United States is preparing for significant strikes on Iran after Tuesday's midterm elections, with Gulf states warned that operations could begin as soon as Wednesday. President Trump and Prime Minister Netanyahu have discussed restarting the strikes, and the military has drawn up plans awaiting Trump's order, with reporting suggesting a large conventional bomb previously used in Afghanistan could be deployed. Tucker Carlson has claimed the administration may be days from a nuclear strike on Pickax Mountain in central Iran, where Israeli intelligence says enrichment has restarted, and that J.D. Vance and Steve Witkoff are advising against it while Netanyahu presses for it; no evidence has been presented for the nuclear claim. Iran has warned of a significant response, and reporting indicates Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth could be blamed if the operation goes badly.

Senator Chris Murphy hospitalized with stroke days after calling Iran war plan insane

tags: politics, war, health
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell, @ericmoutsos

Senator Chris Murphy of Connecticut suffered a stroke and is expected to make a full recovery, according to his chief of staff. Last week Murphy said publicly that he had been briefed in a classified setting on plans for renewed military operations against Iran, describing the plan as insane and warning it would lead to devastating escalation and the likely destruction of the country's commitment to the rule of law. He referred to open reporting on civilian infrastructure that may be targeted, and said he did not know whether those who drafted the plan at the president's request believed it would work.

White House account disputes that delayed vote counts are normal ahead of midterms

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas

An official White House rapid response account responded to a PBS News post explaining that election-night results are often incomplete by asserting that this is not normal. Vote tallies do change as more ballots are counted, and some states take longer to count certain ballots, meaning results in many races may not be known on election night without affecting their legitimacy. The exchange came a day before Tuesday's midterm elections.

Haley Stevens endorses Republican Mike Rogers in Michigan Senate race

tags: politics, elections
sources: @groundnews, @hunteralexanderhowell, @oafnation_actual, @total.hypocrisy

Representative Haley Stevens endorsed Republican Mike Rogers for Michigan's US Senate seat on Sunday, hours after appearing with him at a Detroit church service, having lost the August Democratic primary narrowly to Abdul El-Sayed. Stevens, who has criticised El-Sayed over his comments on Israel and has received substantial funding from pro-Israel groups, defended the switch to CNN's Anderson Cooper, saying she had made her own decision, and described the departure of her chief of staff and other aides as a transition. Reporting cited by critics says Rogers's campaign team includes a registered foreign agent of Israel, and former Michigan governor Jim Blanchard said Stevens's fiancé, Jason Turkish, had chastised her at a dinner over her earlier endorsement of El-Sayed. Representative Debbie Dingell, who had organised a joint appearance that Stevens pulled out of, called the interview one of the most painful she had watched; the race could decide control of the Senate.

Trump says he would preemptively pardon Elon Musk and aides

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas, @groundnews

President Trump said he would protect Elon Musk and would consider preemptive pardons for aides and allies if Democrats pursue investigations after the midterm elections, telling the "Pod Force One" podcast, "It's talk. But if it is talk, we'll have to protect them," and adding, "I would if I needed to. Sure," while invoking his past January 6 pardons. Democrats are preparing wide-ranging investigations into Musk's businesses and his work at DOGE should they take control of the House. Musk has spent close to $500 million opposing Democrats this election cycle. Trump also expressed interest in seeking a third term while acknowledging that "the language is very exacting" on constitutional restrictions.

Senate Democrats report says Trump corruption raises consumer costs

tags: politics, markets
sources: @aaronparnas

Senator Elizabeth Warren outlined a new report from Senate Banking Democrats arguing that President Trump's conduct in office has directly raised costs for Americans. The report points to companies that donated to Trump's inauguration subsequently having lawsuits dropped, an estimated $1.4 billion made by Trump and his family through cryptocurrency ventures, approval of the Paramount-Skydance merger fifteen days after Paramount paid Trump $16 million to settle a lawsuit against CBS, and the abandonment of a rule requiring airlines to compensate passengers for delays and cancellations. An earlier April analysis put the cost of rescinded consumer programs and rules at more than $86 billion a year, and a separate tracker estimates families are paying an additional $3,772 because of inflation.

Republicans brace for internal fight over expected midterm losses

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas

Republicans are privately blaming President Trump for losses they expect across the House and Senate, according to Politico and other outlets. Internal criticism focuses on Trump targeting members of his own party rather than opponents, which some argue has put Senate seats in play alongside the House. Steve Bannon has warned that Republicans may go through a civil war after the midterms given the infighting.

Epstein survivor urges voters to back accountability in midterms

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Anouska DeGeorgiou, who says she survived Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell, released a message to voters ahead of Tuesday's midterm elections. She said she has spoken out and testified but cannot vote in the United States, and asked voters to consider who is protecting women and children, who is demanding accountability even when it involves their own friends, and who keeps making excuses. She asked people to vote on behalf of survivors who cannot.

More than a dozen killed in shootings across at least seven states over 48 hours

tags: health, policing
sources: @aaronparnas

More than a dozen people were killed and over 60 injured in shootings across the United States over a 48-hour period spanning the weekend, with at least seven states affected and 11 mass shootings recorded by the Gun Violence Archive. In Dallas, four people were killed and 15 injured in multiple shootings according to the Associated Press, while one person was killed and eight injured outside the Magic City Classic football game in Birmingham, Alabama. In Florida, a 17-year-old girl and a 20-year-old man were killed in unrelated shootings at Halloween parties that injured at least 11 others. Shootings also occurred near college campuses in Delaware, Illinois and Arkansas, including at a Spirit Halloween store, with further incidents reported in Michigan, Mississippi, Kansas, Texas and California.

Hezbollah rebuilding military capability with Iranian funding, Reuters told

tags: war, politics
sources: @groundnews

Hezbollah has spent three months rebuilding its military capabilities using tens of millions of dollars from Iran, Lebanese security sources told Reuters. The group is acquiring explosives, manufacturing attack drones and rebuilding command systems despite Israeli forces occupying villages in southern Lebanon and growing demands that it disarm. Iran also provided $200 million to support displaced Shiite families. Hezbollah's March 2 attacks in support of Iran prompted an Israeli offensive that killed more than 4,000 people and displaced a quarter of Lebanon's population; fighting eased under a June ceasefire but Israeli strikes continue.

Houthis claim drone attacks on Saudi airport and radar site

tags: war, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Yemen's Houthis said on Monday that they had launched drones at Dammam airport, an early-warning radar installation in Jizan and a military transport aircraft at Jizan airport, according to Reuters. There was no immediate confirmation from Saudi authorities. The claim comes amid an escalation in Houthi attacks on the kingdom.

War in Iran has cost US taxpayers over $47 billion this year

tags: war, markets
sources: @oafnation_actual

A report released by the Associated Press puts the cost of the war in Iran to American taxpayers at more than $47 billion this year alone, excluding the loss of service members' and foreign civilians' lives and the effects on inflation and fuel prices. Comparisons drawn from the figure include roughly $11 billion to end homelessness through rent subsidies, about $28 billion to replace lead pipes nationwide, free pre-K for nearly 4 million children at about $12,000 each, and quadrupling federal cancer research funding, which currently stands at about $7.35 billion a year. American medical debt, the leading cause of personal bankruptcy, stands at about $220 billion.

Cyberattack hits supermarket refrigeration systems across Europe

tags: tech, security
sources: @aaronparnas

A cyberattack targeted refrigeration systems in supermarkets across several European countries including Sweden, Belgium, Luxembourg and Estonia, forcing stores to dispose of spoiled food. The attacks were widespread and occurred over the same morning in multiple countries. Responsibility has not been established. The incident follows an earlier attack this year on refrigeration systems in France, which targeted older equipment, whereas the systems hit in this case are of a different and newer type.

Pentagon support for Navy families evacuated from Bahrain to lapse

tags: defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Support for roughly 1,300 families evacuated from Naval Support Activity Bahrain will end on November 30, Navy leaders told families in a town hall, according to audio obtained by MS NOW and reported by Military.com. A Pentagon official said about $10 million in safe haven allowances has been paid since February. The Pentagon has declined to extend further aid.

Pope Leo XIV becomes first pope to vote in a US election

tags: politics, elections
sources: @groundnews

Pope Leo XIV cast a mail-in ballot in Illinois' midterm elections, the Vatican said, making him the first pope to vote in a US election. Leo retains American citizenship and is registered to vote in New Lenox, Illinois, despite residing in Vatican City. The Holy See Press Office said he expresses his belief in the right and duty of citizens to participate in democratic processes. Voting records show he participated in both Democratic and Republican primaries before becoming pope, and he has criticised President Trump over immigration and foreign policy, with Trump in April calling him weak on crime and terrible for foreign policy.

Learjet carrying nine crashes in Palm Beach County

tags: media
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell, @oafnation_actual, @total.hypocrisy, @ericmoutsos

A Learjet 60 with nine people aboard crashed in a residential area of Palm Beach County, Florida, on Sunday at about 12:50 p.m., according to the FAA and local fire rescue. The jet had taken off from Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas bound for North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas. Early reporting points to an icing incident in severe weather causing a sharp deviation before descent, and leaked audio from the flight has circulated online. Florida Governor Ron DeSantis told CNN the video of the crash "looked like a missile going down," and online claims that the crash was a missile strike or staged event have spread without supporting evidence.
